cards.text: The LORD has just finished giving Moses, Israel's leader, the laws for the offerings (Leviticus 7:37-38). Now He tells Moses to take Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), and Aaron's sons, plus their garments, the anointing oil, a bull for the sin offering, two rams and a basket of unleavened bread. Friend, that's not a to-do list, that's MOVING DAY.

cards.question: Along with Aaron, his sons and all those supplies, Moses also has to gather people at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. Who?
True or false: Moses asks the LORD for a few more days to get everyone ready.

cards.text: With everyone gathered, Moses says, "This is what the LORD has commanded to be done." Then he brings Aaron and his sons up in front of the WHOLE crowd, no pressure, Aaron.

cards.question: Before any fancy clothes go on, Moses washes Aaron and his sons with ___.

cards.text: Then comes the outfit, and it is a LOT of outfit: tunic, sash, robe, ephod, woven band, then the breastpiece with the Urim and Thummim placed inside. Friend, I wear ONE apron and I still tie it crooked.

cards.question: Last comes the turban on Aaron's head. What does Moses set on the front of it?

answers.text: A gold plate called the holy diadem
Two onyx stones set in gold
A golden bell and a pomegranate

cards.text: Next, Moses anoints the tabernacle and everything in it with the anointing oil to consecrate it. Then he heads for the altar, and friend, he is NOT done with that oil.

cards.question: Moses sprinkles some of the anointing oil on the altar ___ times.
Aaron is standing there in the full outfit while the oil goes on the tabernacle and the altar. True or false: Moses pours some of the anointing oil on Aaron's head too.

cards.text: Then it's the sons' turn, and Moses brings them forward and dresses them too, just as the LORD commanded him.

cards.question: Moses dresses Aaron's sons just as the LORD commanded him. What does he put on them?

cards.text: Now the offerings begin, and Moses brings the bull near for the sin offering. One bull, two rams and a basket of bread are waiting, friend, and the bull goes FIRST.

cards.question: Aaron and his sons lay their ___ on the head of the bull for the sin offering.

cards.text: Moses slaughters the bull and, with his finger, puts some of its blood on all four horns of the altar. Not three, not most of them, ALL FOUR, and the rest gets poured out at the base.

cards.question: Why does Moses put the bull's blood on the altar?

answers.text: To mark it as Aaron's alone
To warn people not to come near

cards.text: Then Moses burns the fat on the entrails, the lobe of the liver and both kidneys with their fat on the altar. That still leaves a WHOLE lot of bull, friend.

cards.question: What does Moses do with the rest of the sin offering bull, its hide and flesh and dung?

answers.text: Gives it to the people to eat

cards.text: Then comes the ram for the burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons lay their hands on its head. One bull down, two rams to go, friend, and that basket of bread is STILL sitting there waiting its turn.

cards.question: Moses slaughters the burnt offering ram. Where does he splatter its blood?

answers.text: On all sides of the altar

cards.question: Moses cuts the burnt offering ram into pieces and burns the head, the pieces and the fat. What does he do with its entrails and legs?

answers.text: Washes them and burns them too

cards.text: After that comes the other ram, the ram of ordination, and Aaron and his sons lay their hands on its head. Moses slaughters it, and friend, this is the ram where things get PERSONAL.

cards.question: Moses takes some of the ordination ram's blood and puts it on Aaron. Where does it go?

answers.text: His right earlobe and right thumb and right big toe
His forehead and both hands and both feet
His chest and both shoulders and his back

cards.question: True or false: Only Aaron gets the ordination ram's blood on him, and his sons skip this part.

cards.text: Then this ram's blood goes on all sides of the altar, same as with the first ram.

Next, Moses takes the fat and the right thigh. From the basket of unleavened bread before the LORD, he takes one cake of unleavened bread, one cake made with oil and one wafer, and places them on top.

cards.question: Moses puts the fat, the thigh and the bread into the hands of Aaron and his sons. What happens to it all next?

answers.text: It's set on the golden table

cards.question: True or false: After the wave offering, Aaron and his sons get to keep the fat, the thigh and the bread.

cards.text: Then Moses takes the breast, his own portion of the ram of ordination, and waves it before the LORD, as the LORD commanded him. Even the man running the whole show gets a portion today, friend.

cards.question: Next, Moses takes some anointing oil and some blood from the altar. He sprinkles them on Aaron and his sons and on their ___.

cards.text: Then Moses tells Aaron and his sons to boil the meat at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting and eat it right there with the bread from the basket of ordination offerings. FINALLY, friend, after all that, somebody gets to eat.

cards.question: True or false: Moses tells Aaron and his sons to burn up whatever meat and bread is left over.

cards.text: Then Moses gives them a stay-put order: they must not go outside the entrance to the Tent of Meeting for seven days, until the days of their ordination are complete. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, so trust me, I know a stay-put order when I hear one.

cards.question: Moses says everything done today was commanded by the LORD to make ___ on behalf of Aaron and his sons.
Moses tells Aaron and his sons to stay at the entrance day and night for seven days and keep the LORD's charge. Why does he say they must?

answers.text: So that they will not die
So the people can watch them
So they can rest before serving

cards.question: Seven days at the entrance, with orders from the LORD through Moses. True or false: Aaron and his sons do everything the LORD commanded through Moses.

cards.text: The timer's still running on this one, friend, and I'm not pulling the tray out yet. This story's not over.
